a:r.a:t: Mapping of Haplotypes Can Identify Ancestral Migration Paths

p:cNvPr.descr: A world map showing human migration patterns. The continents are white and the sea behind is blue. A key to the right shows the color codes of the migration lines on the map. The key is labeled “approximate first appearance of marker (kya)”. The colors and number are: orange = 60; light orange = 50; yellow = 45; light green = 40; dark green = 35; light blue = 30; dark blue = 25; dark purple = 20; pink = 10. The origin, represented by a red dot, is on the eastern side of Africa. There is an orange line going up and left from the origin labeled M60, and a darker orange line going down labeled M91. A light orange line goes up from the origin, labeled 169, then splits into two orange lines which move down and right, then reconvene, then diverge around northeastern Asia; this line is labeled M174. The orange line that stays out to sea is labeled M130. There is a small divergent arrow from this line that ends with no label. This orange line arches up to far northeast Asia, then continues east for some time before sloping back down the western US. From the light orange origin line, there are 2 short yellow lines labeled M96 and M89. Connected to these are two purple lines. One curves down and left and is labeled M2; the other curves up and right and is labeled M35. The yellow line to the right splits into two pink lines above. One curves down and left and is labeled M172 and M304; the other is higher up and curves slightly up and left, and is unlabeled. A third line splits off from the yellow M89 line. It is blue, curves up and left and is labeled M170. Splitting off the yellow line is a light green line going to the right, across southern Asia. It is labeled M9. Another line splits off the M89 line. It is blue and labeled M69; a purple arrow diverges upward from this line and it labeled M201. The green M9 line has a divergent blue line going downward toward southern India, labeled M20. A dark green line diverges up from the M9 line, through central Asia. A light blue line labeled M343 splits off to the left through Europe; a pink line labeled M17 splits down and left to western Asia. From the dark green line through central Asia diverges a pink line labeled M45; it curves up and left into the Scandinavian countries. Toward the top, it is labeled LL722. The final divergence from the central Asian dark green line is a long purple line labeled M242. It curves up through Russia to the right, across a narrow channel, and down through midwestern North America, where it turns pink and is now labeled M3. It travels all the way down through central and south America.
